title: Tell the Coordinator what needs to ship
description: Describe an outcome in plain language. The Coordinator asks what it needs, proposes a plan when one helps, and starts the work.
note: A Coordinator panel and new-work entry exist; the outcome-first Factory home is being built.

title: Durable Work Items
description: Every job keeps its goal, plan, state, branch and evidence, so it survives restarts and can be picked up again.

title: Several jobs, several projects, at once
description: Run work in different repositories side by side, within the limits you set.
note: Concurrency limits and a queue exist; priority scheduling is next.

title: Scheduling that respects capacity and dependencies
description: Jobs wait for the machine, the environment or the job they depend on, instead of colliding.

title: Council for hard decisions
description: Ask several models to challenge a plan or a diagnosis before work starts.

title: Plans you can read, edit and approve
description: Turn an outcome into steps, see what changed between plan versions, and approve before anything runs.

title: Steer a running job
description: Pause, redirect or stop a job, or take it over by hand.

title: Scheduled and recurring work
description: Run checks and maintenance jobs on a schedule.

title: Diagnosis after repeated failure
description: When fixes keep failing, the job stops retrying and re-examines its premise.

title: Clone by URL or open a local repository
description: Bring in a private company repository, an open-source project or a folder already on your machine. No fork required.
note: Clone by URL and opening a local folder work; browsing your GitHub and GitLab repositories is planned.

title: Fork & Clone for contributing upstream
description: Fork a project you want to contribute to and clone your fork in one step, when you choose to.

title: Environment Discovery
description: Detect how a project runs, Docker Compose, native Rails, Node or Python, or a mix, and start it with health checks.
note: Discovers and runs real projects on the host today.

title: Reusable Environment Recipes
description: Save a verified way to start, seed and test a project, and reuse it for every job.

title: An isolated VM per Work Item
description: Each active job gets its own environment with its own branch, services, test database and preview.
note: A VM backend passes an isolation test on macOS; linking it to Work Items is next.

title: Repository access without sharing your Git credentials
description: Isolated jobs receive the code they need without your Git credentials being copied into them.

title: Live preview of a running job
description: Open the app a job is building while it works.

title: Claude Code as a Factory worker
description: Use the Claude Code you are already signed in to on your machine as a worker in Factory jobs.
note: Run end to end with a real Claude Code session.

title: Codex as a Factory worker
description: Use your signed-in Codex CLI as a worker.
note: Tested against a stand-in; no live run yet.

title: Gemini CLI as a Factory worker
description: Use your signed-in Gemini CLI as a worker.

title: One Vekrun MCP bridge to the isolated environment
description: Coding CLIs stay signed in on your machine; their commands, file changes and tests run inside the job's environment through one Vekrun bridge.

title: Coding CLI versions and health
description: See which coding CLIs are installed, their versions and whether they are signed in.
note: Detected for Claude Code and Codex.

title: Install and update coding CLIs
description: Install or update Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and GitHub CLI where the vendor supports it.

title: Automatic model routing
description: Pick a capable model for each task, including a lighter one only when it is good enough and available.
note: For API connections.

title: Fallback when a provider hits its limit
description: Hand a task to another provider safely when one reaches its limit.
note: One fallback at a turn boundary exists.

title: Vekrun Context Handoff
description: Rebuild a task's state from its journal, environment and memory so another agent or a restart picks up where work stopped.

title: Claude, OpenAI and Gemini APIs with your own keys
description: Connect a provider account, test it and set a budget. Keys stay in your system keychain.
note: Tested against recorded responses; live runs pending.

title: OpenRouter as a first-class gateway
description: Reach many models with one account, with approved models, providers, privacy and budget policies. Billed by OpenRouter.
note: Tested against recorded responses; live run pending.

title: Local models with Ollama and LM Studio
description: Detect local runtimes, pull and remove models, and route suitable work to them.
note: No live model run recorded yet.

title: See what leaves your machine
description: Preview what a model request will send before it is sent.

title: Jira, Linear, Asana, GitHub and GitLab work on one Board
description: Assigned tickets and issues across your repositories in one place.
note: Tested against recorded responses; no live run yet.

title: Two-way status and field mapping
description: Keep ticket status and pull request review in step with configurable mappings, where the provider supports them.

title: Production incidents on the Board
description: Sentry, Honeybadger, Datadog and AppSignal errors become work you can investigate and fix.
note: Tested against recorded responses; no live run yet.

title: One shared Work Item per incident
description: Duplicate alerts become one Work Item linked to the original events, a ticket and the job.

title: Configurable workflows
description: Decide what happens when an incident or ticket arrives: create a ticket, draft a plan, or start an authorized Factory job.
note: A visual workflow builder exists.

title: Investigate and fix production errors
description: Go from an error to its likely cause, a plan and a fix in a job.

title: Check the fix in production
description: After a deploy, watch whether the error stops.

title: One Inbox for the decisions that need you
description: Approvals, questions, permission requests and blocked jobs, each with why it needs you and what happens next.

title: Pull request reviews in the Inbox
description: Review requests from GitHub and GitLab next to everything else waiting on you.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

title: Approval policies
description: Choose which actions need a person: merges, production commands, spend above a threshold.

title: Independent verification
description: A separate verifier checks the work against the goal, not the agent that wrote it.

title: Quality gates from test evidence
description: Structured test results decide whether work can move on.

title: Proof Packs
description: Tests, screenshots, browser runs, the exact revision and reviewer notes, attached to the pull request.

title: Verification Profiles and Feature Maps
description: Describe what must keep working in a project so every job checks it.

title: Browser checks, screenshots and video
description: Exercise the running app in a browser and keep the evidence.

title: Pull requests prepared with evidence
description: Open the pull request with the plan, results and links, ready for review.

title: A journal of every job
description: A timestamped record of what was decided, run and changed.

title: Searchable Engineering Memory
description: Ask why something was done and get the decision, the ticket and the change.
note: Execution history and scoped memory exist; search is being built.

title: Engineering Insights
description: Pull requests merged, bugs fixed, features delivered, delivery time, rework and spend, over 24 hours to all time.

title: Budgets and cost tracking
description: Spend limits that jobs cannot exceed, with actual cost where the provider reports it.

title: A background Host
description: Vekrun keeps running jobs after you close the window.

title: Keep Host Awake
description: While the Host runs it prevents idle sleep, even with no jobs, so it stays reachable. The screen can still turn off; lid and power settings stay with your OS.

title: Run jobs on another machine you own
description: Add a machine over SSH and send work to it.

title: Vekrun Mobile for iOS and Android
description: Pair securely with your own Host to assign work, follow jobs, answer the Inbox and read Proof Packs.

title: Self-hosted Teams Coordinator
description: A shared Coordinator and organization data store on your infrastructure.

title: SSO included
description: Single sign-on for your organization, included in Vekrun Teams.

title: Organization roles and permissions
description: Decide who can start work, approve, merge and change policy.

title: Shared Board and incident intake
description: One Board and one stream of incidents for the whole team.

title: Shared Factory queues on your workers
description: Team jobs run on machines your organization owns and approves.

title: Team-wide Engineering Memory and Insights
description: Shared history and reporting, stored on your servers.

title: Organization audit
description: An organization-wide record of approvals and consequential actions.

title: Licensing and updates
description: Buy, renew and update a Teams licence. Until this exists nothing can be bought.

title: CI runs linked to the work
description: See GitHub Actions and GitLab pipeline results for a job and repair failures.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

title: Deployment observation
description: Link a deploy to its change and watch production signals afterwards.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

title: Security findings become reviewable fixes
description: Scanner findings become investigations and fixes that a person approves.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

title: Authorized deployment actions
description: Deploy actions only under explicit policy and approval. Never silent production deploys.

title: Terminal, tabs, splits and SSH
description: Take over a job by hand, locally or on a remote machine.

title: Code and diff view with language servers
description: Inspect the change a job made, with diagnostics.

title: AI review of local changes
description: Ask for a review before you open a pull request.

title: AI review of a teammate's pull request
description: Findings on someone else's pull request, posted only when you choose.

title: Windows and Linux checked by hand
description: Everything verified on real Windows and Linux machines, not only macOS.

title: Signed installers
description: Signed builds for macOS first, then Windows and Linux.

title: Guided first run
description: Install, connect your CLIs, import a repository, validate its environment and assign your first outcome.
note: A first-run flow exists in the development build.
